title: DDoS Mitigation Explorer
description: Interactive p5.js simulation of DDoS attack and defense. Adjust botnet size, attack rate, attack type, and amplification reflector, then toggle BCP38 ingress filtering, anycast, scrubbing, and rate limiting to see how much traffic still reaches the origin server's bandwidth and CPU.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity
chapter_title: "Advanced Network Defense: Wireless, DNS, and Zero Trust"

learningObjectives: Analyze how ingress filtering, anycast, scrubbing, and rate limiting each reduce attack traffic.
Distinguish how volumetric attacks load bandwidth while application-layer attacks load CPU.
Reason about why a defense effective against one attack type may be useless against another.
educational.prerequisites: Basic networking (IP, requests per second) and the idea of a botnet.

controls: Slider: attack rate per bot (1-100 req/s)
Select: amplification reflector (None, DNS 50x, NTP 500x, Memcached 50,000x) - volumetric only
Checkboxes: BCP38 ingress filter, anycast (3 PoPs), scrubbing center, rate limiting
pedagogical.assessment: Students find a configuration that keeps legitimate-requests-served above 50% for each attack type and explain why.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing a single defense stops all DDoS.
Assuming rate limiting works equally well against highly distributed botnets.
